augustine.name: Augustine of Hippo
augustine.bio: Bishop of Hippo and Doctor of the Church; the most influential Latin Father.

chrysostom.name: John Chrysostom
chrysostom.bio: Archbishop of Constantinople and Doctor of the Church, famed for his preaching ("golden mouth").

athanasius.name: Athanasius of Alexandria
athanasius.bio: Bishop of Alexandria and Doctor of the Church; defender of the divinity of Christ at and after Nicaea.

cyril-jerusalem.name: Cyril of Jerusalem
cyril-jerusalem.bio: Bishop of Jerusalem and Doctor of the Church; author of catechetical lectures.

irenaeus.name: Irenaeus of Lyons
irenaeus.bio: Bishop of Lyons, martyr and Doctor of the Church; defender of apostolic tradition against Gnosticism.

jerome.name: Jerome
jerome.bio: Translator of the Latin Vulgate and Doctor of the Church.

ambrose.name: Ambrose of Milan
ambrose.bio: Bishop of Milan and Doctor of the Church; teacher of Augustine.

origen.name: Origen
origen.bio: Alexandrian biblical scholar; hugely influential on interpretation, though some of his teachings were later condemned. Read with care.

gregory-the-great.name: Gregory the Great
gregory-the-great.bio: Pope and Doctor of the Church.

hilary-of-poitiers.name: Hilary of Poitiers
hilary-of-poitiers.bio: Bishop of Poitiers and Doctor of the Church.

basil-the-great.name: Basil the Great
basil-the-great.bio: Bishop of Caesarea and Doctor of the Church.

cyril-of-alexandria.name: Cyril of Alexandria
cyril-of-alexandria.bio: Bishop of Alexandria and Doctor of the Church.

the-venerable-bede.name: The Venerable Bede
the-venerable-bede.bio: English monk, historian and Doctor of the Church.

rabanus-maurus.name: Rabanus Maurus
rabanus-maurus.bio: Benedictine abbot and Archbishop of Mainz; biblical commentator.

theophylact.name: Theophylact of Ohrid
theophylact.bio: Byzantine archbishop and commentator on the Gospels.

thomas-aquinas.name: Thomas Aquinas
thomas-aquinas.bio: Dominican friar, theologian and Doctor of the Church; compiler of the Catena Aurea.

catherine-siena.name: Catherine of Siena
catherine-siena.bio: Dominican tertiary, mystic and Doctor of the Church.

teresa-avila.name: Teresa of Ávila
teresa-avila.bio: Carmelite reformer, mystic and Doctor of the Church.

brother-lawrence.name: Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection
brother-lawrence.bio: Carmelite lay brother in Paris; not canonized.

edersheim.name: Alfred Edersheim
edersheim.bio: Jewish-born scholar who became an Anglican priest; wrote on the Temple, the Gospels and rabbinic background. A Protestant writer of the 19th century, used here for historical background, not Catholic doctrine.

ignatius-loyola.name: Ignatius of Loyola
ignatius-loyola.bio: Basque soldier turned priest; founder of the Society of Jesus and author of the Spiritual Exercises.

julian-norwich.name: Julian of Norwich
julian-norwich.bio: English anchoress at Norwich; her Revelations of Divine Love is the earliest surviving book in English by a woman. Venerated, not formally canonized.

francis-de-sales.name: Francis de Sales
francis-de-sales.bio: Bishop of Geneva, Doctor of the Church, and patron of writers; teacher of a holiness for ordinary life.

therese-lisieux.name: Thérèse of Lisieux
therese-lisieux.bio: Carmelite nun of Lisieux, known as the Little Flower; Doctor of the Church, patron of the missions.

anselm.name: Anselm of Canterbury
anselm.bio: Benedictine abbot of Bec and Archbishop of Canterbury; Doctor of the Church, 'father of scholasticism'.

thomas-a-kempis.name: Thomas à Kempis
thomas-a-kempis.bio: Canon regular of the Brethren of the Common Life at Mount Saint Agnes; author (traditionally) of The Imitation of Christ. Not canonized.

walter-hilton.name: Walter Hilton
walter-hilton.bio: English Augustinian canon at Thurgarton, spiritual guide and author of The Scale of Perfection. Not canonized.

council-trent.name: Council of Trent
council-trent.bio: The ecumenical council that commissioned the Roman Catechism for parish priests, published under Pius V in 1566.

baltimore-council.name: Third Plenary Council of Baltimore
baltimore-council.bio: The assembly of the American bishops that ordered a single national catechism, published in 1885.

council-nicaea-i.name: Council of Nicaea I
council-nicaea-i.bio: The first ecumenical council of the undivided Church (325).

council-constantinople-i.name: Council of Constantinople I
council-constantinople-i.bio: The second ecumenical council of the undivided Church (381).

council-ephesus.name: Council of Ephesus
council-ephesus.bio: The third ecumenical council of the undivided Church (431).

council-chalcedon.name: Council of Chalcedon
council-chalcedon.bio: The fourth ecumenical council of the undivided Church (451).

council-constantinople-ii.name: Council of Constantinople II
council-constantinople-ii.bio: The fifth ecumenical council of the undivided Church (553).

council-constantinople-iii.name: Council of Constantinople III
council-constantinople-iii.bio: The sixth ecumenical council of the undivided Church (680–681).

council-nicaea-ii.name: Council of Nicaea II
council-nicaea-ii.bio: The seventh ecumenical council of the undivided Church (787).

leo-xiii.name: Leo XIII
leo-xiii.bio: Pope from 1878 to 1903; author of Rerum Novarum and of encyclicals on Thomism, Scripture, the Church and the state.

pius-x.name: Pius X
pius-x.bio: Pope from 1903 to 1914; canonized 1954. Reformed catechesis and the liturgy, and condemned Modernism.

pius-ix.name: Pius IX
pius-ix.bio: Pope from 1846 to 1878; defined the Immaculate Conception and convened the First Vatican Council.

council-vatican-i.name: First Vatican Council
council-vatican-i.bio: The twentieth ecumenical council, which defined papal primacy and infallibility and issued the constitution on faith and reason.
